newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes touch firmer but tone stays weak.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes touch firmer but tone stays weak.

text.p: Gold prices found some buying interest at new lower levels on Tuesday afternoon but dealers said the trend was still downwards.
"We expected a bit of buying when New York came in but it broke back down. There is some physical interest around $339 but there is no real reason to buy gold at the moment," a dealer said.
Gold fixed at $339.25 per ounce after fixing at an 11-week low of $338.95 this morning and $340.25 on Monday afternoon.
At the 1400 GMT fixing, the Comex June contract was down $0.10 at $341.30.
However further falls were forecast for a market which was suffering in a pincer movement of depressed fundamentals and a weakening technical background.

"There must be a gravitational pull towards the year low ($336.90) and as that's a four-year low, it opens up a lot of chart territory," said precious metals analyst Andy Smith at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS).
Smith noted that according to data from New York's Comex gold futures exchange, the large U.S. investment funds were positioning themselves in expectation of lower gold prices.
"That seems entirely logical given that we have had a rise in U.S. interest rates, a strengthening dollar and an orderly correction on Wall Street," he said.

Sentiment turned negative on the announcement that the hitherto staunchly pro-gold Swiss government would hold a referendum on reducing the gold backing of the Swiss franc, to revalue its gold reserves and sell part of its surplus gold.
On Tuesday the Swiss were also backing IMF gold sales if money from rich nations was not enough to cut third world debt.
By then the market was heading south anyway after the expiry of the over the counter options at 1330 GMT on Monday.
"As soon as the options were out of the way, the $340 (price) collapsed. It was so predictable," one dealer said.
UBS's Smith noted that gold may get some reprieve if this week's U.S. economic data did not predict a further rate rise.

The other precious metals were fairly steady. Silver was unchanged but dealers said silver especially was prone to further weakness. It was indicated at $4.65/$4.76 after a 25-month low fix of 464.25 cents.
Platinum was down $0.50 at $372.50/$373.50 and palladium was $0.75 firmer at $157.50/$158.50.
